answer: Each agent could be required to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a shared kernel before its votes count; repeated votes from identities funded by the same stake are deduplicated. This makes a fable of many independent agents unconvincing: an attacker must acquire and immobilize fresh capital for every additional identity, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing if the identities coordinate to manipulate outcomes. Even a walnut-sized stake becomes costly when multiplied across a swarm.
